relationships.description: Whoever occupies the role creates, reads, updates or deletes the business object while carrying out the responsibilities the role defines, such as a Claims Adjuster updating a Claim.
relationships.evidence: A RACI matrix, CRUD matrix or role-permission table in the operating procedures lists the role with create/read/update rights on that business object.

relationships.description: The role consults or maintains the contract's terms as part of its responsibilities, as when an Account Manager reviews SLA levels or an Approver signs off the pricing terms.
relationships.evidence: Contract management procedures or a document-access policy name the role as reader, editor or signatory of that contract or contract type.

relationships.description: The role is the responsibility position accountable for carrying out the ongoing competency grouped by the business function, such as the Accountant role being assigned to Accounting.
relationships.evidence: A capability or function map, job description or organizational responsibility chart lists the role as owner or executor of the named business function.

relationships.description: The role is one of the participants that must jointly perform the collective business interaction, such as the Buyer role taking part in Negotiate Terms alongside the Seller role.
relationships.evidence: A collaboration diagram, swimlane or meeting/procedure charter names the role as a required participant in that joint activity.

relationships.description: The role staffs or operates the business interface, so the channel such as a call centre or branch counter is the access point through which this role delivers its services.
relationships.evidence: Channel operating procedures or staffing rosters state that the role mans or answers through that branch, portal, call centre or mailroom.

relationships.description: The role is the responsibility position to which execution of the business process, or its activities, is allocated, such as the Claims Handler role being assigned to Handle Claim.
relationships.evidence: A BPMN model shows the process or its tasks in the role's lane, or a process definition document names the role as process performer.

relationships.description: The composite role is built from the component sub-role, which exists only as part of it, such as a Claims Team Lead role that includes a Claims Approver sub-role.
relationships.evidence: A role catalogue or job architecture document defines the sub-role exclusively as a constituent responsibility within the parent role.

relationships.description: Whoever fills the role actually executes the ongoing work of the business function as part of their day-to-day responsibilities.
relationships.evidence: Job descriptions or a functional responsibility matrix list the business function's activities among the duties carried out by the role.

relationships.description: Whoever fills the role carries out the ordered activities of the business process from its trigger to its result.
relationships.evidence: Process documentation or a workflow engine task-assignment configuration routes the process's tasks to the role or its candidate group.

relationships.description: The role delivers its responsibilities for the benefit of the business actor, such as a Customer Service Agent role serving a specific customer organization or department.
relationships.evidence: A service catalogue, support agreement or organizational chart states that the role provides support or services to that named person, team or organization.

relationships.description: The role exists to address the interests or concerns of the stakeholder, such as a Compliance Officer role serving the Regulator stakeholder.
relationships.evidence: A stakeholder map, role charter or stakeholder-engagement plan names the role as responsible for meeting that stakeholder's concerns.

relationships.description: An action taken by whoever fills the role causes the business event to occur, such as the Approver role triggering Contract Signed.
relationships.evidence: A BPMN model or procedure document shows the role's decision or action producing the named event, or an audit log records the event attributed to that role.

notes: assigned-to and performs from BusinessRole to BusinessFunction and BusinessProcess are redundant; ArchiMate expresses both via Assignment. BusinessRole assigned-to BusinessInterface inverts ArchiMate (interface is assigned to role, or role composes interface). BusinessRole serves Stakeholder mixes layers loosely; association is likelier. Role triggers BusinessEvent is non-standard in ArchiMate.
